_read: SINGLE SOURCE of the request cycle. A state machine written more than once — a server module,
browser scripts, a triage page — comes out similar, not equal: different labels in each copy,
seven transitions on one side and eleven on the other, one copy ignoring the rule that an admin's
request is born approved (the same request showing as 'Approved' in the panel and 'Awaiting
triage' in the triage). Changing the cycle would cost one commit per copy, and nothing would warn
So the API and the agent's tool read THIS file, and the JavaScript computes no state at all —
it receives one from the API. Change it here, and it changes everywhere.
The KEYS and the STATES are English (docs/GLOSSARY.md). `label` and `short` are what the CLI
prints next to a state, in the engine's default language; the reviewer's screen resolves
_initial_for_admin: Owner and admin do not triage themselves (design decision, 2026-09-17).
_states: label and short are read by the CLI only; the core never reads them, and the browser reads engine/locales/.
_transitions: Approved NEVER goes back to rejected: to change something approved, a new request with data.related.
_accepts_supplement: A supplement on a rejected request, or on a question, sends the request back to 'open'.
_request_categories: `doubt`, and not `question`, on purpose: `question` is already a STATE of the cycle (the owner
asks whoever requested). They are different concepts, and both travel as loose text — the same
name for the two would make a grep lie and let a bug through unnoticed.
`bug` is a CATEGORY, not a system of its own (docs/BUGS.md): a bug is the documentation and the
behaviour disagreeing, and that is already a request against a block, with a snapshot, an author
and a cycle. The three outcomes of triage — the system is wrong, the doc is wrong, the doc has a
hole — do NOT exist yet: today a bug request walks the same cycle as every other.
`page` asks for documentation that does not exist yet, in plain words: the request hangs on the
page it was asked from, and the agent that applies it writes a NEW page (see `brief` in
engine/cli/agent.ts). It walks the same cycle too: a text nobody approved is not a lock, whoever
`dependency` is `holdrim propose-deps`'s own category (engine/cli/propose.ts, issue #43): two
blocks that share a glossary term and declare no data-depends on one another, so it is worth a
human looking. It walks the same cycle as every other request — approving one is not writing the
data-depends itself, only agreeing a human should add it by hand.
